content: Latakia tobacco is a uniquely processed type of tobacco that was originally produced in Syria and derives its name from the port city of Latakia. Currently, the majority of Latakia tobacco is produced in Cyprus. The tobacco undergoes a curing process over a fire made from stone pine or oak wood, which imparts a distinctive, intense smoky and peppery flavor and aroma. Due to its strong characteristics, it is not typically smoked on its own but is instead used as a condiment tobacco, particularly in English, Balkan, and some traditional American tobacco blends. Although Cypriot Latakia tobacco is widely available in the current tobacco market, the use of Syrian Latakia in boutique tobacco blends has significantly declined in recent years. This decline can be attributed to a warehouse fire in late 2004 that destroyed nearly the entire stock of Syrian Latakia held by Cornell and Diehl, a prominent manufacturer of pipe tobacco blends, including those under the G.L. Pease brand. The fire obliterated tons of this rare and highly prized tobacco, leaving only a few scattered pounds remaining. The loss was devastating not only for the manufacturers but also for the importer, who owned the majority of the destroyed stock. The business impact was severe, as all Syrian Latakia-containing blends from both G.L. Pease and Cornell & Diehl could no longer be produced. The remaining inventory on store shelves represents the last of these blends for the foreseeable future. Efforts to replenish the supply of Syrian Latakia have been hindered by the sensitive nature of trade relations with Syria. While every possible channel is being explored to replace the lost stock, there is no clear timeline for when another shipment might become available. Despite this setback, other manufacturers, such as McClelland and Mac Baren, have managed to continue producing pipe tobacco blends that include Syrian Latakia.
